questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why people should stop buying plastic bottles
A new way of recycling plastic using enzymes
How plastic reached the top of Mount Everest
Why landfill is the best way to deal with waste
questions.why: Beth says they'll hear about chemical recycling, a groundbreaking way of making old plastic new again.

questions.q: Where does Neil say microparticles of plastic have recently been found?
options: Only in the oceans
Inside people's homes
In fresh rainwater in cities
At the top of Mount Everest
questions.why: He says “At the top of Mount Everest!”, though Beth's guesses are also true.

questions.q: What happens to most plastic waste around the world?
options: Less than 10% is recycled and about half goes to landfill
Most of it is recycled
Almost all of it is burnt
It is sent back to the companies that made it, to be reused
questions.why: Neil says less than 10% gets recycled and about half goes straight to landfill.

questions.q: What problem with mechanical recycling does William Kremer describe?
options: It is much too expensive for most poorer countries around the world
It releases dangerous gases
The plastic loses quality and becomes more brittle each time
It only works on drinks bottles
questions.why: He says it loses a bit of quality each time and becomes slightly more brittle.

options: Plastic is melted down and pressed into new shapes and forms
Plastic is buried with special leaves
Plastic is burnt to produce energy
Enzymes break plastic into basic parts to make new plastic
questions.why: Beth says enzymes break plastic into its basic building blocks, used to make new plastic.

questions.q: Where did researcher Sintawee Sulaiman find the LCC microorganism?
options: In the sea near Osaka
In a pile of rotting leaves in a park
Inside an old plastic bottle in her lab
In a rubbish dump
questions.why: On an autumn walk in the park, she found it in a pile of rotting leaves.

questions.q: What does William Kremer mean when he says the discovery was “not the end of the story but the beginning”?
options: LCC was already ready to be used in factories around the world
The discovery was a mistake
LCC was promising but needed much more development
Scientists lost interest in LCC
questions.why: He says LCC showed promise but needed a lot more work to become stable and effective.

questions.q: What do scientists in France plan to do by 2025?
options: Recycle 50,000 tonnes of plastic waste a year
Recycle all of the world's plastic waste every year
Stop producing nylon clothes
Ban PET drinks bottles
questions.why: Neil says they plan to recycle 50 thousand tonnes of plastic waste annually.
